subject: Data agreement options & role mapping — Novex follow-up

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Data agreement options & role mapping — Novex follow-up

Hi Emma — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so your contracts team has what they need: 

Summary from the call:
- Novex confirmed the primary use-case: patient intake form ingestion and model-assisted triage (PHI will be limited to contact details + clinical notes excerpts).
- You indicated Novex plans to be the Controller for customer/patient records; Redwood would be a Processor for inference and storage of transient inference context. Please confirm if that remains the plan.
- SOC 2 posture: you asked whether we have a recent Type II attestation and whether we can share a summary relevant to data handling and encryption-in-transit/at-rest.
- Cross-border transfer concern: you referenced EU patients in pipelines and asked about SCC modules we support.

What I’m attaching: Redwood_SOC2-brief.pdf (summary of scope & attestation date) and an initial DPA skeleton we typically use — see Novex_DPA_review.docx (draft). Also attached is an SCC-module high-level comparison (SCC-module-comparison.xlsx) to make module tradeoffs explicit.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Can you confirm the Novex contracting contact (Contracts email in To line ok)?
2) Please confirm Controller/Processor alignment (one-line confirmation is fine) so our legal team can mark the DPA accordingly.
3) Contracts reviews DPA doc and flags changes — we’ll follow with a redline call next week if helpful.

If helpful, I can loop in our Security lead (Aditya) for any technical clarifications on SCC choices and SOC 2 scope. Would you like that on the thread?

Thanks — aiming to keep this to a 1-week review window so we can lock terms before the procurement kickoff.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai

Thanks Priya — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications before our contracts team dives in: 

> - Novex confirmed the primary use-case: patient intake form ingestion and model-assisted triage (PHI will be limited to contact details + clinical notes excerpts).

Yes, that is correct. PHI will be limited to name, DOB, limited clinical notes excerpts and a contact phone number.

> - You indicated Novex plans to be the Controller for customer/patient records; Redwood would be a Processor for inference and storage of transient inference context. Please confirm if that remains the plan.

We want to be explicit: Novex is Controller. Redwood as Processor for inference and ephemeral storage only. For logs/telemetry that contain hashed identifiers, we need to confirm the retention policy.

A few asks from our side: 
- Can you send the SOC 2 Type II report or a redacted letter ASAP for our security review? We may not need the full report yet but want attestation date and scope.
- SCC modules: we usually prefer modules that include a healthcare/data protection addendum; can you recommend which of your modules map to a HIPAA-sensitive workload?
- Contracts contact: contracts@novexhealth.com is correct for procurement.

If you can get Aditya on a short call this week to confirm the SCC recommendation and retention options for telemetry/logs, that would be great.

Thanks,
Emma Clarke
Head of Integrations
Novex Health
emma@novexhealth.com

--

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data agreement options & role mapping — Novex follow-up (SCC & retention notes)

Priya / Lauren — adding a few technical / compliance notes that I recommend we surface to Novex in our DPA draft and in the SCC comparison spreadsheet: 

1) SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II attestation with a period ending 2027-11-30. We can provide a redacted SOC 2 summary letter (control scope, auditor, and tests performed). Recommend sending the Redwood_SOC2-brief.pdf as the initial artifact; full report can be provided under NDA if requested.

2) SCC modules: For Novex’s stated workload (healthcare + EU subjects), I recommend we present two SCC paths in the comparison: 
   - Option A (recommended): Core SCC + Healthcare Addendum — covers standard transfer safeguards and a healthcare-specific addendum that clarifies PHI protections and breach notification timelines. This is the faster path for customers who want explicit HIPAA-oriented terms.
   - Option B (restrictive): Full Restricted Transfers (stricter) — for customers with additional requirements (e.g., public sector or Germany-specific rules).

3) Controller/Processor: We should mark Novex as Controller and Redwood as Processor in the primary DPA. For logs/telemetry that contain hashed identifiers, propose a short retention window (30 days) and explicit deletion scope in the DPA; if Novex wants longer telemetry retention for analytics, include that as an optional addendum with opt-in toggles.

4) Draft DPA: I reviewed the skeleton Priya attached. I’ll prepare two redline flavors: one DPA with Option A default and one with Option B language ready. Also prepping an SCC-module-comparison.xlsx that maps each module to common Novex asks (retention, encryption, subprocessors).

5) Next steps: Priya to send initial packet to Novex (SOC2 brief, DPA skeleton, SCC comparison). I’ll be on the kickoff call if they want us to walk through SCC choices.

Aditya Rao
Security & Compliance Solutions
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
